items.summary: The NVIDIA Board of Directors announced it is initiating an independent investigation after reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has become the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, will oversee the inquiry. The Board stated it prioritizes national security but said it has no reason to believe any secrets were compromised.
items.title: NVIDIA Board Launches Independent Investigation Into Jensen Huang Allegations

items.summary: Nvidia said on Sunday it is initiating an independent investigation after reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The inquiry follows New York Times allegations in October that he had a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Singapore-based executive suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China as a Chinese spy. A draft email seen by Reuters shows Huang admitting to an affair and taking responsibility for his actions. Nvidia did not immediately respond to comment on the Axios report.
items.title: Nvidia Launches Probe After Report CEO Was Foreign Intelligence Target

items.summary: Nvidia's board announced Sunday it is launching an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation. Nvidia also published a message from Huang admitting he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed. Huang apologized to his family and colleagues. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.
items.title: Nvidia launches investigation into Jensen Huang amid spy reports

items.summary: Lee Lung Nien, Citi’s country officer and head of banking for Singapore, says the sector risks losing wealthy clients to slow onboarding. He drives private banking account opening times down to within one month by end-2026 from about six weeks or longer. Nearly half of new accounts opened June–August 2026 at PBIG member banks were done in a month. Lee stresses balancing speed with risk controls, warning that five-day openings are unsafe and shutting the door entirely kills business. Citi Singapore’s cross-border activity grew 18% from August 2025 to August 2026; inflows supported by Citi rose 22%. The bank plans to reskill 85% of banking operations staff into redesigned roles by 2028 and hire around 100 private bankers globally, with much in Asia.
items.title: Citi Singapore Chief Targets Faster Private Banking Onboarding

items.summary: In The Straits Times’ askST Jobs series, business correspondent Timothy Goh asks whether it is illegal to secretly record a performance appraisal meeting. Certified senior professional Jayanthi Arun of the Institute for Human Resource Professionals says covert recording can damage trust and may breach company policies or confidentiality obligations. Employment lawyer Amarjit Kaur of Withers KhattarWong adds that no general law in Singapore automatically makes secret recording unlawful, but it could still breach an employment contract, company policy, confidentiality duties, or the trust expected at work, potentially amounting to misconduct serious enough to justify dismissal without notice.
items.title: Singapore lawyers weigh in on secretly recording appraisal meetings

items.summary: In a message titled "A Message to Our Company," NVIDIA's chief executive apologized publicly, saying he was unfaithful to his wife. He said the betrayal hurt her and their children and that there is no excuse. Addressing colleagues, board members, partners and shareholders, he took full responsibility for what he did and accepted criticism. Regarding national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation, which he supports.
items.title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Apologizes for Infidelity and Addresses Security Concerns

items.summary: In its Sunday newsletter dated Nov 8, 2026, the Tech Policy Press describes Tuesday’s midterm elections as an extraordinary repudiation of President Donald Trump and his party. Democrats earned a huge House majority, a solid Senate advantage, six flipped governorships and state legislative majorities that ended Republican control held since 2010. The outlet frames tech issues — AI, data centers, billionaire influence over the economy and politics — as more salient than ever. NBC exit polls found 56% of voters cited AI and data centers; CBS polling showed opposition to local data centers breaking toward Democratic candidates. Victory speeches from Sherrod Brown, J.B. Pritzker, James Talarico and others emphasized accountability for tech money. Experts convened in a podcast and public events, including remarks by Data & Society executive director Janet Haven calling the outcome “a real moment for change,” while Jenna Ruddock of Free Press cautioned that “the road ahead is uncertain.” The newsletter then rounds up related coverage on Anthropic’s IPO, children’s online safety, AI governance, European data-center protests and platform democracy issues. The piece presents these as Tech Policy Press reporting rather than verified election facts, distinguishing the outlet’s editorial framing from cited polls and expert views. It offers no picture plan because a graphic would only decorate prose that already conveys the narrative in words; figures are embedded throughout without needing visual encoding.
items.title: Tech Policy Press Frames US Midterm Results as a Turning Point for Tech Democracy

items.summary: Tech Policy Press covered a panel marking the launch of Freedom House's annual Freedom on the Net report, which analyzed internet freedom in 38 countries covering about 71% of global users. Kian Vesteinsson, deputy director of research at Freedom House, said this year marked the 16th consecutive year of decline and that Iran saw the steepest fall amid an 88-day nationwide shutdown during military strikes. He noted similar patterns in Russia as both governments built domestic alternatives to the global internet. The report found age assurance laws proposed or passed by policymakers in 10 countries, with experts warning these measures carry privacy risks because they rely on sensitive data processing. Panelists from the Internet Society and Proton VPN emphasized that online safety framing is being used to justify undermining encryption and collecting personal information. Jennifer Brody of Freedom House recommended countering shutdowns through transparency, expanding satellite internet, funding censorship tools, protecting children through platform design rather than identity checks, and centering human rights in AI decisions. Mahsa Alimardani highlighted hope despite the decline, pointing to Bangladesh's first year without a shutdown since 2016 under an interim government that took power after Sheikh Hasina was ousted in August 2024.
items.title: Freedom House Panel Reviews Global Internet Freedom Decline and Age Checks

items.summary: A Democratic sweep in the midterm elections could reshape U.S. energy policy, though sweeping change is unlikely given veto power and the need for Republican support on appropriations. Democrats controlling Congress and key committees would seek to curb Trump administration fossil fuel and data center expansion, restore clean energy tax credits, regulate AI-driven demand, and investigate oil deals involving Venezuela and Russia’s Putin. In Texas, Jon Rosenthal became the first Democrat on the Railroad Commission since 1990. Analysts at TD Cowen lowered the odds of a bipartisan permitting bill passing to about 25%, from 40% before the election.
items.title: Democratic Midterm Win Set to Reshuffle U.S. Energy Policy

items.summary: Several countries are racing to develop space-based solar power (SBSP) systems that harness near-constant sunlight in orbit and beam it to Earth. On Earth, solar output is limited by night, cloud cover, atmospheric conditions and seasonality; roughly 30 per cent of incoming radiation never reaches the ground. SBSP places microwave-transmitting satellites in geostationary orbit about 35,000 km up to power large reflectors on the surface. China’s Zhuri programme, the U.K.’s Space Solar project and Japan’s OHISAMA aim to develop the technology first. The U.K. government has provided around $1.6 million for its demonstration missions. In January, SpaceX applied for FCC permission to launch 1 million satellites for SBSP; Overview Energy announced plans in April to beam 1 GW by 2030 to Meta’s data centres. Supporters say it could accelerate clean power deployment, while opponents call the technology exorbitantly expensive and highly uncertain, with commercial deployment now expected between the 2030s and 2050s.
items.title: Space-Based Solar Power Race Gains Momentum With New Satellite Plans

items.summary: Nvidia said it launched an independent investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted on Sunday to having an extramarital affair with a Chinese executive suspected of spying for Beijing. He will remain CEO pending the outcome and wrote in a company-wide letter that he was unfaithful to his wife and deeply sorry. The disclosures follow reports that US officials feared Nvidia acted as a backdoor for export-controlled chips.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Admits Extramarital Affair With Suspected Chinese Spy

items.summary: A financial horoscope dated November 9, 2026 presents daily predictions across twelve zodiac signs regarding money, work, and business. For Cancer, it says the sign will respect managerial instructions and maintain focus on new matters, with an improved work pace. Aries is described as favourable for increased opportunities and profit; Taurus faces mixed results while focusing on contracts; Gemini expects normal routine with rising profits; Leo sees good prospects for wealth; Scorpio must exercise caution amid possible income and expense increases; Sagittarius shows signs of increased profit but should follow rules; Capricorn anticipates growth in prosperity and savings; Aquarius gains momentum toward financial success; Pisces may face higher expenses and is advised to avoid industry matters. The piece notes that astrological predictions are the opinions of an astrologer, based on planetary positions, and that BT disclaims responsibility for any suggestions made.
items.title: Daily Financial Horoscope Offers Predictions for Cancer and Other Signs

items.summary: Business Today asks how much retirees can withdraw monthly without depleting savings, noting that withdrawing too fast leaves people vulnerable while withdrawing too little compromises quality of life. Shruti Oke, SVP and Head of Product Management at Tata AIA Life Insurance, said the amount should depend on expected expenses, inflation, retirement age, healthcare needs, other income and corpus duration rather than corpus size alone. She outlined estimating post-retirement expenses against pension or annuity income, then factoring in inflation and longer life expectancy. Oke described a systematic withdrawal plan as one option that structures regular cash flows while the remaining corpus stays invested but does not guarantee longevity of funds. Tata AIA Shubh SIP offers automatic withdrawals from age 60 under its Retirement/Whole Life option.
items.title: Tata AIA Expert Outlines Retirement Withdrawal Strategy

items.summary: Nvidia announced on Sunday (Nov 8) that it is launching an independent investigation after a New York Times report alleged its CEO Jensen Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive accused of passing information to Beijing. A committee of independent directors and outside counsel will oversee the review, which Nvidia says has no basis for believing national security or company secrets were compromised. Top Republican lawmakers have called on Huang to brief Congress this month about the report. In an employee message, Huang admitted being unfaithful to his wife and said he took full responsibility.
items.title: Nvidia Launches Probe Into CEO's Alleged Foreign Intelligence Ties

items.summary: Nvidia announced it is launching an independent investigation into reports that its CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. The company said the probe would be overseen by independent directors and legal counsel, while Mr Huang will keep his role. Nvidia noted Mr Huang admitted to staff he had such a relationship.
items.title: Nvidia Launches Investigation Into CEO's Alleged Affair With Chinese Spy

items.summary: The Nvidia board announced an independent investigation, assisted by outside counsel, into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The inquiry follows disclosures that Secretary of State Marco Rubio reviewed a spring 2026 memo about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang of Singapore-based Megaspeed, which federal authorities have investigated over alleged illicit semiconductor exports to China. Board members stated they have no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised and said Huang will continue leading the company.
items.title: Nvidia board launches independent probe into foreign intelligence targeting of Jensen Huang

items.summary: Professor Michal Pędziwiatr, one of two surgeons who treated victims on the street after a mass shooting in Krakow, spoke to the BBC about his experience. Two doctors were eating near Main Market Square when a gunman began firing at random, killing six and injuring 15. The pair rushed into the area to begin their rescue before emergency services arrived.
items.title: Krakow Surgeon Describes Treating Shooting Victims for BBC

items.summary: The world's largest telecoms firm, Huawei, is on trial in New York. It faces accusations of stealing American technology and evading US sanctions. Audio from the proceedings will be available later today.
items.title: Huawei Faces Trial in New York Over Technology and Sanctions Allegations

items.summary: Two Polish police officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, both under 30, were injured while pursuing and detaining a 24-year-old suspect who killed six people and wounded 17 in an attack on Saturday. Police arrived at the main square just 23 seconds after the first emergency call. Prime minister Donald Tusk said they likely saved many lives by risking their own.
items.title: Two Kraków police officers hailed as heroes after confronting gunman

items.summary: Amisha Padnani, writing for The New York Times, suggests running races as a way to experience cities more deeply. She shares tips on choosing events that pass through varied neighborhoods and planning logistics like transportation and lodging. Contributors Unjin Lee and Theodora Yardley describe how support crews and downtime enhance the trips. Padnani concludes she does not feel truly visited a place unless she has run it.
items.title: Running Races as a Way to Experience Cities

items.summary: Residents and visitors returned to a shooting site in Kraków, where bullet marks remained on café windows and candles marked the six killed. The attack occurred Saturday 7 November when a 24-year-old gunman opened fire in Poland's second-largest city. Witnesses filmed people running for cover as emergency services rushed to the area.
items.title: Kraków Reopens After Deadly Shooting That Killed Six

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV ended his first trip to Uruguay in nearly four decades by praising the women who have passed on the Catholic faith, telling mothers and grandmothers never to tire of it. He attended Mass for at least 50,000 worshippers in Florida’s main square, though the Vatican estimated attendance at 50,000 against a city population of about 40,000. His homily also addressed gender-based violence, noting nearly 20,000 femicides across Latin America over five years.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV closes Uruguay visit with tribute to women

items.summary: Footage shows derailed carriages after a fatal train collision in northern Egypt that killed at least seven people and injured dozens. One train was travelling from Giza to the Fayoum oasis, south west of Cairo, while another headed from Cairo to Aswan. Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said an investigation is underway and would hold accountable anyone who proves their negligence.
items.title: Egyptian President Orders Probe After Fatal Train Crash

items.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres strongly condemned a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland that killed six people and injured 16, his spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said. The attack occurred Saturday afternoon near Main Market Square when an armed assailant opened fire on civilians. Polish prosecutors launched a terrorism investigation Sunday into the shooting, which also claimed three victims found at the suspect's residence. Guterres expressed deep shock and offered condolences to families and Poland.
items.title: UN Chief Condemns Deadly Krakow Mass Shooting

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extra-marital affair with Alice Huang, CEO of Singapore-based Megaspeed. In a letter to employees obtained by Axios, he apologized and accepted responsibility for hurting his family. Nvidia's board said it launched an independent investigation after reports that customers called Megaspeed were passing information to Chinese spies. The board stated it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised and expressed confidence in Huang's leadership.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Admits Affair, Board Launches Security Review

items.summary: A new agricultural research centre opened at the University of California, Davis in May 2026, following a $50 million pledge announced by philanthropists Lynda and Stewart Resnick in October 2022. The donation was the university's largest from individual donors at the time, with around $40 million funding facility development and $10 million creating the Resnick Agricultural Innovation Research Fund to support projects on agricultural materials such as pistachio shells and pomegranate residues. Co-owners of The Wonderful Company, the couple also pledged $750 million to Caltech in 2019. The completed centre spans approximately 34,000 square feet across two storeys and is described by UC Davis as LEED-certified and all-electric with solar power.
items.title: Resnick Gift Opens UC Davis Agricultural Research Centre

items.summary: The Waghoba Habitat Foundation (WHF), founded by Sanjiv Valsan, has grown from a tree-planting group formed during the Covid-19 lockdown into an initiative linking forest conservation with tribal livelihoods. Working across Aarey Forest and Chinchwadi near Karjat, WHF consults Adivasi communities on planting grafted fruit trees alongside native species such as Mahua, which Valsan says once made up nearly 30 per cent of their diet but takes about 12 to 13 years to bear. The foundation's wild foods lab turns forest produce into products like Mahua butter and pickles, creating income while preserving biodiversity.
items.title: Waghoba Habitat Foundation Blends Indigenous Knowledge With Forest Conservation in Aarey

items.summary: On Sunday evening Delhi's instantaneous AQI stood at 371 in the 'very poor' category. Of the 59 stations reporting data at 7 pm, 19 were 'severe', seven 'poor' and 33 'very poor'. The worst reading was 460 at Jahangirpuri; the day's average settled at 376. Social media users reported smelling smoke and hazy conditions. Experts attribute the deterioration to firecrackers, vehicular emissions and peak stubble burning, with air quality forecast to turn 'severe' on Monday.
items.title: Delhi Air Turns Very Poor as Diwali Firecrackers, Stubble Burning Stack Up

items.summary: Iranian media suggested Saturday evening explosions in southern Iran stemmed from Iranian military activity rather than US strikes, though officials had not confirmed missile attacks on territory including Qeshm Island. Both sides reported vessel hits near the Strait of Hormuz; UKMTO monitors described an incident about 18 nautical miles east of Khor Fakkan with unknown damage and unclear link to a reported US attack. Reuters could not confirm any strikes.
items.title: Iran Disputes Blast Origins as Shipping Strikes Continue Near Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: Thousands of earthen lamps lit up Srinagar's Lal Chowk on Sunday evening, with tourists and local residents gathering around the historic Ghanta Ghar clock tower to mark Diwali. Hindus and Muslims joined in lighting diyas and firecrackers. Ankush Chatterjee, a tourist from Kolkata who spoke to PTI, said he was delighted to celebrate the festival in Kashmir.
items.title: Diwali lights brighten Srinagar's Lal Chowk as tourists and locals celebrate

items.summary: A major fire broke out around 9:30 PM in an open plot belonging to Rashmi Builders in the Mohak City area of Virar East, triggered by firecrackers. Firefighters from the Vasai-Virar City Municipal Corporation (VVMC) rushed to the site and brought the blaze under control. No casualties or injuries were reported, though vegetation and surrounding areas were completely charred.
items.title: Fire Breaks Out In Open Plot At Mohak City

items.summary: Delhi's air quality reached 'very poor' status with an AQI of 371 Sunday evening, driven by firecracker emissions during Diwali. Of 59 monitoring stations, 19 recorded 'severe' readings at 7 pm and 33 were 'very poor', while Jahangirpuri hit the highest level at 460. The day's average AQI of 376 rose from Saturday's 369. The Air Quality Early Warning System forecasts conditions could worsen to 'severe' from November 9, citing firecrackers, vehicle exhaust and stubble burning amid poor ventilation.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Hits Very Poor on Diwali

items.summary: A Punjab consumer commission ordered the Railways and IRCTC to refund ₹10,620 to a passenger who missed his train after its departure time was allegedly advanced without proper intimation. The Ferozepur District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission also directed payment of ₹5,000 as compensation for mental agony, harassment and litigation expenses. The commission held that failing to inform passengers about revised timings amounts to deficiency in service, rejecting the Railways' claim of passenger negligence.
items.title: Punjab Consumer Commission Orders Railways and IRCTC Refund for Passenger Who Missed Train

items.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation arrested a government official and a private individual over an alleged bribery case involving the clearance of imported containers at the Plant Quarantine Station in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. The CBI alleges that Assistant Director Sudhakara TM demanded ₹1 lakh from a private firm to expedite approval, accepting it through intermediary Sunkavalli Satyanarayana during a trap laid on November 6. Both were produced before a court on November 7.
items.title: CBI Arrests Official and Private Individual in Visakhapatnam Bribery Case

items.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the Uttar Pradesh government of inaction in the Ram Temple donation theft case and questioned Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s silence, asking who would take responsibility. His remarks followed a day after Adityanath demanded an apology over the 1990 firing on kar sevaks ahead of Yadav’s December 12 temple visit. The donation theft case has seen eight arrests, a chargesheet filed before an Ayodhya court on September 23, and reported findings of 105 instances of unauthorised cash removal; police recovered Rs 79. 85 lakh from seven accused.
items.title: SP Chief Questions CM Silence Over Temple Donation Theft Case
